title: Outlier Detection Methods MicroSim
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Apply the Z-score rule and the IQR rule to the same data, move the two thresholds, and see which points each rule flags and where the rules disagree.

educational.topic: Outlier detection with Z-scores and the IQR rule
learningObjectives: Students will be able to apply the Z-score rule and the IQR rule to a dataset, adjust their thresholds, and explain why the two rules can flag different points.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with immediate feedback, comparing two methods on the same data
keyQuestions: In the ages data, why does the Z-score rule miss an age of -5?
The skewed incomes are all valid. Should the values the IQR rule flags be removed?
What happens to the number of flagged points when a threshold is lowered?
commonMisconceptions: A flagged value is an error (a flag only says the value is unusual, and it may be valid data).
The Z-score rule and the IQR rule always agree (they are built on different statistics and often disagree).
The mean and standard deviation are safe yardsticks (the outliers themselves pull the mean and inflate the standard deviation).
assessmentOpportunities: Given a list of about ten numbers with one extreme value, students compute the IQR fences, state which values the IQR rule flags, and explain in words why a Z-score threshold of 3 might fail to flag a second, smaller outlier.
